A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoGo research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference-time measurements, adapter-selection analyses and ablation experiments across multiple model families.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, cross-domain evaluations, scalability measurements and adapter-quality, rank and interference analyses.

M1.justification: The probe pass, norm or inverse-entropy scoring, top-k selection, normalized signal weights and output-based merging remain unchanged in Equations 1–6 and Algorithm 1. Added implementation explanations and experimental variants do not establish a revision to LoGo itself.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds GSM8K, MedQA and WritingPrompts for domain-specific adapter training and cross-domain evaluation, extending coverage to mathematical reasoning, medical QA and creative writing under domain mismatch. The original main benchmarks, CodeXGLUE and CNN-DailyMail evaluations remain.

E2.justification: AdapterSoup is newly evaluated in Tables 1–3, and the unadapted Base model is added to the CodeXGLUE comparison in Table 2. LoRARetriever's fusion variant is removed from all three comparisons, while its mixture variant remains.

E3.justification: V3 introduces component-control settings, adapter-pool scaling measurements, mixed well-trained/under-trained pools, and a 45-adapter experiment using 15 datasets, ranks 8/16/32 and norm-based top-10 selection. Figure 3's reported backbone changes from Qwen-2.5-32B to DeepSeek-LLM-7B-Base. The original main training recipe, splits and selection defaults remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test top-1 selection, uniform weighting, similarity-based selection, probe scalability, domain mismatch, adapter quality, rank variation and negative alignment between selected adapters. Existing token, layer and adapter-count studies remain. The original mixture-versus-fusion ablation is retained in Appendix E.2 rather than removed.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices explicitly report a single run because the fixed adapters and signals are deterministic. V3 adds no repeated-seed evaluation, confidence intervals or significance tests; the existing boxplot reporting practice remains.

E6.justification: Shared Table 1 scores are unchanged, but new comparator entries alter rankings: AdapterSoup scores 42.5 on LLaMA BBH versus LoGo's 38.3/40.0. V3 also adds Tables 5 and 7 and scalability/robustness findings, including 6.8 GB of adapter parameters and 126.7 MB of probe activations for 260 adapters. Fusion-baseline results disappear, and Figure 3 is replaced.

T1.justification: New Appendix B adds a first-order Taylor expansion and Cauchy–Schwarz bound, Equations 7–8, motivating update norm as a proxy for potential loss influence. This is a limited derivation, without a guarantee of task relevance or an analogous entropy bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free instance-level adapter selection and merging, competitive or better performance, gains up to 3.6%, and comparable inference throughput. The additional studies do not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning quality-sensitive selection, rank robustness and limited destructive interference. Its limitations newly discuss inability to disentangle topic/style/skill, increased time to first token for short outputs, and adapter-pool redundancy. These substantially extend the applicability qualifications beyond v1.

D1.justification: V1 promises future code and adapter releases; v3 supplies public code and trained-adapter access links, although Section 4.1 retains future-release wording. V3 also documents disabled KV caching during probing, activation storage and batched tensor operations. These substantially expand reproducibility information; actual online availability is not established by the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive comparisons with K-LoRA, Decouple and Orthogonalize, LoRAtorio and LoRA-Flow, broadening positioning against training-free, data-free and dynamic composition approaches. It distinguishes adapter-pool scope, optimization requirements and per-step costs. AdapterSoup is also newly cited and evaluated.

P1.justification: V3 edits the abstract, introduction and related-work prose, standardizes terminology and adds an appendix overview. It reorganizes the analysis section and moves the merging-strategy discussion into the appendix, while retaining the overall narrative and much existing text.

P2.justification: V3 adds ablation Table 5, cross-domain Table 7 and memory Figure 5, replaces Figure 3's plots, and restructures comparator columns in Tables 1–3. The original merging plot moves from Figure 5 to appendix Figure 11. Existing heatmaps and adapter-selection charts are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the unchanged method easier to assess through broader comparisons, component controls, measured probe costs, clearer limitations and resource links. Benefits are tempered by removed fusion comparisons and overstated interpretations: Section 5.3 claims consistent superiority over top-1 selection, although Table 5 reports BBH scores of 43.3 for top-1 versus 38.3 for LoGo. The net improvement is positive but limited.
